Version 0.4.1 makes rescans of unchanged folders much cheaper, and `ysync service` now manages a daemon that Homebrew started.

The daemon walks every folder when it starts and again on each safety scan, hourly by default. That walk reopened every parent directory from the folder root for each entry it checked. On one Mac with three folders and about 810,000 entries, a restart kept the daemon at roughly 115% CPU for two minutes. Now each entry is checked with one stat through the directory already being listed, and only new or changed entries get the full parent check. An unchanged rescan of a 120,000-file test tree fell from 29.6 seconds of CPU time to 2.2 on a Mac. That is a single trial on a tree that favors the change, and Linux has not been measured. First-time indexing gains less because hashing dominates it. Indexed content, deletion inference and the symlink-parent checks are unchanged.

`ysync service status`, `stop` and `start` used to know only ysync's own service. If you started the daemon with `brew services start ysync`, `ysync service stop` reported a missing service and the daemon kept running. These commands now find Homebrew's definition when no native service is installed and manage that instead, and they say so. `install` refuses while Homebrew's definition exists. `uninstall` leaves it for `brew services stop ysync`.

Nothing changes on the wire, in the index or in configuration, so 0.4.0 and 0.4.1 peers synchronize with each other and you can upgrade one machine at a time: run `brew update && brew upgrade ysync`, then `brew services restart ysync`. Cargo users can install tag `v0.4.1`. Experimental prerelease.
